title: Bradford Protein Assay for Protein Concentration Measurement
author: Daniel C Moreira
materials: Weight 100 mg of Coomassie Brilliant Blue G-250 (e.g., B0770, Sigma-Aldrich) and dilute it in 50 mL of ethanol using a magnetic stirrer at room temperature.
In a fume hood, slowly add 100 mL of 85% (w/v) phosphoric acid (e.g., W290017, Sigma-Aldrich) to the previous solution and homogenize.

Prepare several BSA solutions at concentrations from 0.05 to 0.40 mg/mL 4 using PBS (or the relevant buffer/solvent) in Eppendorf tubes. Example: If your stock solution is 3.94 mg/mL, first prepare a 0.4 mg/mL (50.8 µL to a final volume of 500 µL) and then dilute it serially to 0.20, 0.10, and 0.05 mg/ mL (e.g., 100 µL of the previous solution + 100 µL of PBS). 4 Under the conditions described in this protocol, the change in absorbance at 595 nm is linear within the 0.05–0.40 mg/mL BSA range (see figure below). steps.title: Prepare Bradford reagent solution
steps.instruction: Mix 0.01 % (w/v) Coomassie Brilliant Blue G‑250, 4.7 % (v/v) ethanol and 8.5 % (v/v) phosphoric acid. Dilute the mixture to a final volume of 1 000 mL with distilled water, filter through a Whatman No. 1 paper (or equivalent) and store at room temperature protected from light. Commercial ready‑to‑use reagents (e.g., Bio‑Rad 5000006) may be used as an alternative.

substeps.instruction: Combine the three reagents in appropriate proportions.
Add distilled water to reach 1 000 mL total volume.
Filter the solution through Whatman No. 1 paper.
Store the filtered reagent at room temperature, protected from light.

steps.title: Prepare BSA stock solution
steps.instruction: Make a 4 mg/mL bovine serum albumin (BSA) stock in PBS (e.g., dissolve 6 mg BSA in 1.5 mL PBS). If possible, use the same buffer that will be used for the samples and verify that the buffer components are compatible with the Bradford reagent.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 6 mg BSA (Sigma‑Aldrich A0281).
Add PBS to a final volume of 1.5 mL to obtain 4 mg/mL.
Check buffer compatibility with the Bradford reagent (refer to supplier bulletins if needed).

steps.title: Verify BSA stock concentration
steps.instruction: Measure the absorbance of the BSA stock at 280 nm in a UV‑transparent cuvette and calculate the actual concentration using the appropriate extinction coefficient (example: 50 µL diluted to 1 000 µL gave A280 = 0.130).

substeps.instruction: Dilute an aliquot of the BSA stock (e.g., 50 µL to 1 000 µL).
Record the absorbance at 280 nm.
Calculate the true BSA concentration from the absorbance.

steps.title: Dilute samples to assay range
steps.instruction: Dilute each sample in PBS (or the buffer used for the BSA standards) so that its protein concentration falls within 0.04–0.05 mg/mL (the linear range of the standard curve). If the protein content is unknown, prepare several dilutions and test them.

substeps.instruction: Estimate the sample protein concentration (e.g., rat liver homogenate ~5 mg/mL after a 1:20 tissue dilution).
Calculate the required total dilution factor (e.g., further dilute 1:15 to reach ~0.33 mg/mL).
Prepare at least three different dilutions when the concentration is uncertain.

steps.title: Add water blanks to plate
steps.instruction: Dispense 260 µL of distilled water into at least three wells of a 96‑well microtiter plate; these wells will serve as blanks (auto‑zero/reference).

steps.title: Add BSA standards to plate
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of each BSA standard solution (including a zero‑standard containing only buffer) to at least three replicate wells.

steps.title: Add samples (and dilutions) to plate
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of each diluted sample to at least three replicate wells. For better coverage of the dynamic range, pipette several volumes (e.g., 1 µL + 9 µL buffer, 2 µL + 8 µL buffer, 5 µL + 5 µL buffer, 10 µL alone).

substeps.instruction: Prepare the indicated sample‑buffer mixtures.
Pipette 10 µL of each mixture into the designated wells (triplicates).

steps.title: Add Bradford reagent to wells
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL of Bradford’s protein reagent to every well containing a BSA standard or a sample. Use a positive‑displacement pipette (e.g., Multipette M4, Eppendorf) to avoid bubbles. Do not add reagent to the water‑only blank wells.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 250 µL Bradford reagent into each standard and sample well.
Avoid adding reagent to the blank wells.

steps.title: Incubate plate at room temperature
steps.instruction: Let the plate sit at room temperature for 5 minutes. Read the plate before 1 hour of incubation; precipitation may start after 10–15 minutes at high protein concentrations.

steps.title: Measure absorbance at 595 nm
steps.instruction: Read the microtiter plate at 595 nm using a plate reader (optional additional readings at 450 nm and 590 nm). Perform the measurement within 1 hour of adding the reagent.

steps.title: Calculate average absorbance of replicates
steps.instruction: For each set of triplicate wells (standards and samples), compute the mean absorbance at 595 nm.

steps.title: Generate standard curve and regression
steps.instruction: Plot the average absorbance (Y‑axis) versus the known BSA concentration (mg/mL, X‑axis). Fit a linear regression (Y = a × X + b) using software such as Microsoft Excel.

steps.title: Determine sample protein concentrations
steps.instruction: Use the regression equation to interpolate the protein concentration of each sample from its average absorbance, then multiply by all dilution factors applied earlier. Express results as mg protein per g wet weight when appropriate (e.g., assuming 1 g ≈ 1 mL).

substeps.instruction: Insert the sample absorbance into the linear equation to obtain concentration in the assay mixture.
Apply the total dilution factor (e.g., tissue homogenate dilution × plate dilution).
Convert to desired units (e.g., mg/g wet weight).
